name: Wolfsklamm
kurzbeschreibung: Wolfsklamm in Stans is regarded as the pearl of the Tyrolean Unterland: 354 wooden steps over roaring cascades up to the cliff monastery St. Georgenberg.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Wolfsklamm near the municipality of Stans in the Tyrolean Unterinntal is one of the most spectacular natural gorges in the Northern Limestone Alps and is deservedly hailed as the „pearl of the Tyrolean Unterland“. Over millions of years, the untamed Stanser Bach has carved its way deep into the hard limestone of the Karwendelgebirge. Over a distance of around 1,500 metres, the gorge ascends more than 250 metres in altitude. A boldly engineered trail leads hikers across bridges, galleries, and hundreds of wooden steps past thundering waterfalls and deep emerald pools directly up to Tyrol's oldest pilgrimage site, the cliffside monastery St. Georgenberg.

Nature & Gorge Trail

Wolfsklamm was officially opened on 11 August 1901 following painstaking trail construction led by Tyrolean tourism pioneer Franz Posch. After floods destroyed the walkway structures on several occasions, the path was continuously modernised and secured. The centrepiece of the walk consists of 354 wooden steps anchored into the rock, massive walkways, and solid railings suspended directly above the foaming spray of roaring cascades. The interplay of white frothing water, sheer rock faces, and lush moss creates a unique natural atmosphere. At the upper end of the gorge, the valley opens into a tranquil streambed adorned with countless artfully stacked stone cairns. From there, the path continues across the heritage-protected Hohe Brücke – an architectural masterpiece dating back to 1497, spanning the Georgenberg gorge at a height of over 40 metres as Tyrol's oldest stone arch bridge – up to the Benedictine monastery St. Georgenberg.

Visit & Getting There

Wolfsklamm is open seasonally from early May to early November, daily from 09:00 to 16:30 (weather-related closures reserved in case of heavy rainfall or snowfall). Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): Adults approx. 7,00 €, children (6 to 14 years) 3,00 €, children under 6 years free. The proceeds fund the continuous upkeep of the elaborate wooden walkways. Arrival by public transport: Take ÖBB (S-Bahn S4/S5 or REX) to Stans bei Schwaz station, from where a signposted footpath leads directly to the gorge entrance in approx. 15 minutes. By car: Via the Inntal motorway A12, exit Schwaz or Jenbach, follow the regional road to Stans; paid parking is available at the gorge entrance (Parkplatz Wolfsklamm / Weng).

Tips

Due to the 354 stairs, walkways, and wet ground, the gorge trail is accessible neither for prams nor for wheelchairs; sturdy footwear with non-slip treaded soles and weather-appropriate clothing are essential. For the circular route via St. Georgenberg and the historic Stations of the Cross Maria Tax back to Stans, allow approx. 2.5 to 3 hours of walking time. Stop for a break at the traditional pilgrimage inn Wallfahrtsgasthof St. Georgenberg and enjoy Tyrolean delicacies beneath shady chestnut trees.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Anfang November täglich 09:00–16:30 Uhr geöffnet
